newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin sacks scandal-hit justice minister.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin sacks scandal-hit justice minister.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin on Wednesday sacked Justice Minister Valentin Kovalyov, caught up in a scandal involving a sauna video film, and replaced him with a former national security chief, the Kremlin said.

A Kremlin spokesman said Yeltsin, who had earlier suspended communist Kovalyov pending official investigation, had signed two decrees on the matter. Kovalyov's replacement is Sergei Stepashin, a former head of the FSB federal security service.

Yeltsin suspended his justice minister last Wednesday pending a probe into a newspaper report that alleged Kovalyov had been filmed in a gangland sauna with naked women. Interior ministry officials have said the video film, sections of which have been broadcast on Russian television, was genuine.
But Kovalyov, 53, has implied the film is fake. He asked Yeltsin to suspend him to give him time to clear his name.

Yeltsin sacked Stepashin, 45, from his top security job in June 1995 for mishandling a hostage-taking crisis in the southern Russian town of Budennovsk. At least 120 people were killed in the stand-off, and the separatist Chechen fighters who took the hostages subsequently escaped.
Stepashin has headed the government's administrative department since November 1995. He is married and has one son.
